question.text: What will be the ending value of the UST 10Y Yield for these biweekly periods of Q4 2026? (Nov 23 - Dec 4)
question.resolution_criteria: Each subquestion will resolve as the last available daily value of the U.S. Treasury Securities at 10-Year Constant Maturity published on the [FRED website](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10) for the final calendar day (typically the final Friday) of the corresponding biweekly period.
question.fine_print:
* If the FRED data is delayed, the value will be taken as soon as published for the relevant date.
* If the market is closed on the scheduled ending date or if no value for that date is published by FRED for two weeks, the most recent available value from an earlier day in the period will be used.
* Only the initially published value for each date will be used (no revisions).
* The value is reported in percentage points.

research:
Here is the research summary. I couldn't reach FRED (timeouts), so I used the Treasury yield curve CSV that FRED's DGS10 series is built from.

## 1. Resolution source
- The resolving value is FRED DGS10 for 2026-12-04, a Friday. FRED copies Treasury's daily par yield curve "10 Yr" column. Every attempt to reach fred.stlouisfed.org timed out. [FRED](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10)
- 2026-11-13: the Treasury 10Y close was **5.15%**. This is the latest official value (the code baseline shows FRED at 5.10 for 11-12, which matches Treasury). [Treasury CSV](https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/daily-treasury-rates.csv/2026/all?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2026&page&_format=csv)
- Recent Treasury closes: 11-12: 5.10; 11-10: 4.98; 11-09: 4.88; 11-06: 4.86; 10-30: 4.94; 10-21: 5.13; 10-05: 5.31 (the 2026 high in this file); 09-30: 5.29. [Treasury CSV](https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/daily-treasury-rates.csv/2026/all?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2026&page&_format=csv)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The resolving date is 12 trading days after the latest official print. The current level (about 5.12-5.15) is near the middle of the question's range (4.255-6.255).

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: The 10Y eased about 2-3bp intraday to roughly 5.12-5.13% ahead of a Warsh speech, retail sales and the FOMC minutes. The 2Y was about 4.84-4.85%. [Hindustan Times](https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/us-news/us-treasury-yields-fall-as-investors-await-kevin-warshs-comments-us-retail-sales-data-and-fed-minutes-101794826409019.html); [Rallies](https://rallies.ai/news/treasury-yields-dip-following-weekly-gain-as-stocks-fall-9e483b7499abc201)
- 2026-11-16: The dollar was near a 19-month high on expectations of a Fed hike. The US-Iran war and uncertainty over a deal are keeping oil and yields elevated. [FXStreet](https://www.fxstreet.com/analysis/weekly-forex-forecast-eur-usd-xau-usd-gbp-usd-usd-jpy-bitcoin-and-more-video-202611161502); [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/us-iran-deal-uncertainty-to-weigh-on-rupee-and-bonds-fed-rbi-rate-paths-eyed-ce785ededf8ef226)
- 2026-11-13/15: The 10Y rose 29bp in the week to 5.15%, its biggest weekly rise since April 2025. Drivers were October CPI at +0.4% headline and +0.3% core, plus Waller saying a 50bp hike could be warranted. CME FedWatch reportedly prices about 92% for a 25bp hike on Dec 9 and about 8% for 50bp, with a January hike largely priced. [QNC](https://qncnews.com/2026/11/15/us-ten-year-treasury-yield-ends-week-at-5-15-per-cent-in-biggest-weekly-rise-since-april-2025/); [Stocktwits](https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/what-shaped-us-treasury-yields-and-the-dollar-in-week-ended-november-13/cNb2sojR9Qd)
- Mid-Nov: Trading Economics also cites PPI at about 3-year highs and worries about AI corporate debt after an Nvidia leadership change. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield)
- 2026-10-28: The Fed held at 3.75-4.00% after a September hike. Warsh said the Fed was not on a predetermined path. [CTOL](https://www.ctol.digital/news/fed-holds-10-2-vote-treasury-yields-retrace-december-hike/)
- Early Nov: Democrats made gains in the midterms, and the 10Y briefly fell to about 4.84-4.86% (Nov 5-6). [BusinessLine](https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/markets/g-sec-yields-harden-again-as-inflation-worries-eclipse-global-tailwinds/article71706937.ece)

## 4. Base rates
- Code baseline (15 trading days from 11-12 at 5.10): p5 4.78, p10 4.86, p25 4.97, **p50 5.11**, p75 5.24, p90 5.35, p95 5.43. The real horizon from the 11-13 print is about 14 trading days.
- Realized volatility is high right now. Over the last 3 months, two-week swings of 15-30bp were common: 9-22 to 10-05 went +35bp, 10-21 to 10-30 went -19bp, and 11-06 to 11-13 went +29bp. [Treasury CSV](https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/daily-treasury-rates.csv/2026/all?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2026&page&_format=csv)
- 2026 trend: 4.19 (Jan 2) to 4.64 (Aug 25) to 5.31 peak (Oct 5), then a 4.86-5.15 range in Nov.
- Seasonality, mid-November to early December in past years. These figures are from my memory of FRED and were not checked in this session:
  - 2025: about 4.14 to about 4.14
  - 2024: 4.43 to 4.15
  - 2023: about 4.45 to about 4.28
  - 2022: about 3.69 to 3.51
  - 2021: about 1.63 to 1.34
  - Yields fell over this window in 4 of 5 years, which I'd call a weak pattern. 2026 is running far above all of those years in level.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Kalshi, "Friday Nov 20": ≥5.12 at 59%, ≥5.16 at 46%, ≥5.20 at 28%, ≥5.06 at 79%. The implied median is about 5.15.
- Kalshi, Dec 9 at 2:15pm ET (Pyth feed, which is not FRED): above 5.10 at 58%, above 5.05 at 69%, above 5.01 at 76%.
- Kalshi, year-end Dec 31: ≥5.10 at 57%, ≥5.15 at 53%, ≥5.25 at 46%, ≥5.5 at 15%, ≥5.0 at 90%. The 5.25 price looks inconsistent with its neighbours, so treat the ladder with caution.
- Kalshi, max by Jan 1: ≥5.35 at 43%, ≥5.5 at 17%. Polymarket, max before 2027 at 5.5%: 9.7%. Polymarket, November max: 5.21% at 54%, 5.25% at 35%.
- Trading Economics model: about 5.11 at quarter end and about 4.88 in 12 months. [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield)
- I found no Polymarket or Kalshi contract that resolves on Dec 4 itself.

## 6. Upcoming events before Dec 4
- Nov 16-17: Warsh speech; Nov 17: retail sales and Nvidia earnings; Nov 18: October FOMC minutes. [Rallies](https://rallies.ai/news/treasury-yields-dip-following-weekly-gain-as-stocks-fall-9e483b7499abc201)
- Nov 25 (Wed): October PCE and personal income, per a secondary calendar. I did not check this against BEA. [FinanceCalendar](https://www.financecalendar.com/event/us-personal-income-and-outlays-pce-november-2026/)
- Nov 26: Thanksgiving, markets closed. Nov 27: early bond close.
- Dec 1-3: ISM manufacturing and services, JOLTS, ADP.
- **Dec 4 (resolution day): November jobs report**, per a secondary calendar. I did not check this against BLS. [FinanceCalendar](https://www.financecalendar.com/event/us-employment-situation-non-farm-payrolls-november-2026/)
- Ongoing: news on a US-Iran war or deal (oil), Treasury auctions, and Fed speakers before the Dec 8-9 FOMC blackout begins around Nov 28.
